# Robert Seilbeck: Publicly Documented Professional Activities at revel8

**Research date: November 22, 2026.** This report uses only the supplied public-source material. It distinguishes Seilbeck’s own statements from company descriptions, third-party data, and LinkedIn reposts. Several pages provide no stable publication date; LinkedIn’s relative labels, such as “2y,” are not treated as exact dates.

## Executive assessment

Robert Seilbeck is publicly identified as a **co-founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of revel8**, a company developing security-awareness training focused on AI-enabled social engineering. The strongest evidence for his career transition is his own announcement that he was taking the CTO role at **Company Shield**, revel8’s former name, after nine years at Celonis. Revel8’s company materials identify him as one of its three founders and describe its founding year as 2024. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT); [revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/company/about); [revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

**Assessment:** The record establishes Seilbeck’s senior technical and founding role, but it does **not** establish that he personally designed every revel8 feature, authored its research findings, or presented its conference workshops. His documented public activity is most clearly a career announcement, an organizational relocation-and-hiring announcement, a listed publication byline, and participation in the company’s public professional presence. Company product claims and performance figures should remain attributed to the company or the speaker who made them. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT); [Seilbeck, n.d.-b](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_its-official-revel8s-is-moving-to-munich-activity-7369384059174572035-Zvjg); [revel8, n.d.-b](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert); [Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))

## Professional background and role

### Career transition and founding context

In a first-person LinkedIn post, Seilbeck said he was “excited to take the role of the CTO of Company Shield,” described it as a cybersecurity startup, and said he was leaving Celonis **after nine years**. He characterized the new company’s mission as protecting organizations against AI-generated hacker attacks and invited prospective colleagues to consider its jobs. The supplied rendering labels the post “2y” rather than displaying an exact publication date, so the post verifies the announcement and his stated tenure, **not a precise day or month of departure**. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT))

Revel8 says it was founded in **2024** under the earlier name **Company Shield**. Its funding announcement names **Julius Muth, Tom Müller, and Robert Seilbeck** as founders and describes them as former Celonis employees. This corroborates the broad transition in Seilbeck’s post, although the supplied material does not give a full job-by-job account of his Celonis responsibilities. A third-party company-data page instead lists a **2023** founding year; because that conflicts with revel8’s account and no explanation is provided, 2024 is best reported as the **company’s stated founding year**, not as an independently resolved incorporation date. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/company/about); [revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Crustdata, 2026](https://profiles.crustdata.com/company/company-shield))

Seilbeck’s public LinkedIn profile describes him as a technology leader and co-founder with experience in database systems and engineering. Revel8’s author biography identifies him as CTO and describes expertise in database design, scalable cloud infrastructure, and engineering leadership. These are **public professional descriptions**, useful for understanding how he and the company present his specialization; the supplied sources do not independently document particular database architectures, systems he built, academic credentials, or patents. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882); [revel8, n.d.-b](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert))

| Documented point | What the source establishes | Important limit |
|---|---|---|
| Prior employer | Seilbeck says he spent nine years at Celonis. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT)) | The supplied post does not specify his successive titles or exact employment dates. |
| Founding and leadership | Revel8 names Seilbeck among its founders; its author page calls him CTO. ([revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [revel8, n.d.-b](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert)) | These sources do not assign authorship of every company product to him. |
| Technical specialization | His profile and company biography emphasize databases, cloud infrastructure, and engineering leadership. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882); [revel8, n.d.-b](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert)) | The descriptions are not independent technical evaluations. |

## Publicly announced projects and technical direction

### Security-awareness platform

Revel8 describes its product as training employees against AI-powered social engineering rather than relying solely on conventional, static awareness material. Its LinkedIn company description says it uses AI and open-source intelligence to simulate attacks, including deepfake voice calls and multichannel phishing, tailored to employees’ roles. This is evidence of the **company’s announced product direction**, not proof of every asserted capability’s effectiveness or of Seilbeck’s individual implementation work. ([revel8, n.d.-d](https://www.linkedin.com/company/revel8ai))

The company’s funding announcement frames the project as a human-centered cybersecurity platform intended to prepare employees for AI-based impersonation. It says new funding would support product development, enterprise features, team growth, and international expansion. As a founder and CTO, Seilbeck has a documented leadership connection to that project; the announcement, however, does not identify a specific component that he alone built. ([revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [revel8, n.d.-b](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert))

### Later product announcements and attribution

Seilbeck’s public LinkedIn profile includes a **repost** by another revel8 employee describing an AI module builder. In the example, a customer requested a training module about “ClickFix,” and the employee said the tool generated company-branded, interactive, policy-compliant material for review and publication within minutes. A separate visible post describes “Boosters,” AI-powered follow-up quizzes intended to reinforce lessons after initial training. These posts document **announced capabilities and the claims made about them**. A repost or visible reaction is not evidence that Seilbeck authored the posts, built either feature personally, or independently verified the stated turnaround and learning benefits. Their supplied dates are relative LinkedIn labels, not stable publication dates. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))

The same profile shows a repost about a revel8 demonstration at **Merantix AI Campus DevDay** concerning a next-generation e-learning platform and an AI Module Builder. The person describing the demonstration says **they**, together with a colleague, represented revel8. The material therefore supports that a revel8 team presented the project; it does **not** support calling Seilbeck a DevDay presenter. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))

## Conference appearances, presentations, and interviews

The supplied LinkedIn profile displays Seilbeck reposting revel8 updates from **it-sa – Home of IT Security**. One update advertises a company booth and a workshop with **NVISO Security** on social-engineering techniques; another encourages attendees to visit the booth. These are evidence of revel8’s announced conference participation and Seilbeck’s public amplification of it. They do **not** name him as the workshop’s speaker, provide a recording of his remarks, or establish that he attended in person. The captured text says “3 weeks,” but without a stable posting date that label should not be converted into a precise calendar date. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))

**No verifiable Seilbeck interview or personally delivered conference presentation is identified in the supplied sources.** In particular, unrelated podcast-methodology material and an unrelated YouTube result supplied alongside the relevant pages do not identify him as an interviewee or speaker and are not evidence of his professional activity. The defensible finding is therefore narrower than “he has given no interviews”: **none can be documented from this source set**.

## Published work and the limits of technical attribution

Revel8’s author page lists Seilbeck as the author associated with a **July 24, 2025** item titled *“revel8 is now live on the STACKIT Marketplace – Cybersecurity awareness, built for Europe.”* That listing is evidence of a dated, publicly listed company publication and a marketplace announcement. The supplied extract does not include the article’s full text or a separately verified article URL, so it cannot substantiate detailed claims about the integration’s architecture, hosting arrangements, or Seilbeck’s hands-on engineering contribution. The author page categorizes the item as a **press release**, not a technical research paper. ([revel8, 2025](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert))

His LinkedIn activity page also lists an article titled *“Developing Software and People at the Forefront of Innovation,”* with a relative age label of “5y.” Its title is consistent with an engineering-leadership subject, but the supplied text provides neither its contents nor a stable publication date or separate article URL. It would be inappropriate to infer a specific technical argument, methodology, or research result from the title alone. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT))

A post visible on Seilbeck’s profile discusses an investor’s account of revel8 analysis of **more than 100,000 attack simulations**, including **more than 10,000 vishing calls**, and conclusions about multichannel attacks and realistic messages. Those are **attributed claims in a visible third-party post**, not a technical paper shown to be authored by Seilbeck. The underlying report, its methodology, and its publication date are not supplied. The figures should not be presented as independently audited results or as his personal research findings. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))

## Recent company and organizational announcements

### Funding, customers, and growth claims

Revel8 announced **€7 million in funding** in a company article headed *“revel8 Raises €7M to Fight AI-Powered Cyberattacks.”* It describes a seed round led by **Peak**, names the three founders, and says the company counted **FC Bayern, OBI, and Stihl** among its customers at the time of that announcement. The supplied article extract does not expose an unambiguous publication date. Third-party Crustdata records a **September 2025** seed round of **$6.6 million** and a **July 2024** pre-seed round of **$1.4 million**. These are differently denominated and differently framed figures; the provided material does not fully reconcile the company’s €7 million announcement with Crustdata’s round-level dollar figures. ([revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Crustdata, 2026](https://profiles.crustdata.com/company/company-shield))

Revel8’s LinkedIn description makes broader commercial claims, including work with **seven of the 40 DAX companies** and named organizations such as Allianz, OBI, Stihl, and TSG Hoffenheim. These should be reported as **company-stated customer or adoption claims**, not independently verified contracts, current customer counts, or evidence of Seilbeck’s individual sales activity. ([revel8, n.d.-d](https://www.linkedin.com/company/revel8ai))

### Munich move and recruitment

In another first-person post, Seilbeck announced that revel8 **planned to move to Munich in early 2026**. He advertised junior software engineering, full-stack engineering, customer-success, and senior product-design roles; the full-stack description specifically mentioned building a scalable security-awareness platform. This is direct evidence of his public involvement in communicating hiring priorities and the company’s planned technical expansion. The supplied LinkedIn rendering again uses a relative age label rather than a dependable publication date. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-b](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_its-official-revel8s-is-moving-to-munich-activity-7369384059174572035-Zvjg))

The earlier funding announcement described revel8 as Berlin-based and its Munich relocation as planned. Its current “About us” page says the company is headquartered in Munich. Read together, the pages support the conclusion that **the company now publicly presents Munich as its headquarters**; they do not establish the precise date on which the move was completed. ([revel8, n.d.-c](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/company/about))

Headcount figures likewise require source and timing qualifiers. Revel8’s “About us” page says it has **50** team members; its LinkedIn page displays **77 employees**; and Crustdata’s October 2026 page reports **61** employees. They may reflect different snapshots or counting methods, but the supplied material does not resolve the differences. None is a sound basis for an exact, current employee total as of November 22, 2026. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/company/about); [revel8, n.d.-d](https://www.linkedin.com/company/revel8ai); [Crustdata, 2026](https://profiles.crustdata.com/company/company-shield))

## Conclusion

The most defensible professional profile is of a former Celonis employee who publicly announced his move into the CTO role at Company Shield, is named as a revel8 founder, and has since publicly communicated hiring and relocation plans. Revel8’s own materials connect his role to an expanding AI-focused security-awareness business and list a dated marketplace press release under his author profile. The evidence is **substantially stronger for leadership, announcements, and company affiliation than for individually attributable technical inventions, research publications, conference talks, or interviews**. That distinction is essential: company marketing, reposted colleagues’ updates, and third-party metrics should not be converted into claims of Seilbeck’s personal authorship or independently established product performance. ([Seilbeck, n.d.-a](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_jobs-at-company-shield-activity-7256921894526808065-LVdT); [Seilbeck, n.d.-b](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/robert-seilbeck-a4789882_its-official-revel8s-is-moving-to-munich-activity-7369384059174572035-Zvjg); [revel8, 2025](https://www.revel8.ai/author-robert); [Seilbeck, n.d.-c](https://de.linkedin.com/in/robert-seilbeck-a4789882))
